subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be scoped to reason-bearing dropped-MEDIA diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns persistent configurable root expansion, or should this issue define a new MEDIA-specific root/config policy?
rationale: The safe diagnostic fix is narrower than the broader host-file access policy; choosing a new configurable root surface changes product and security boundaries.

options.title: Diagnostics here, roots in the root-policy item
options.body: Add warn/event and concise user-visible reason handling for dropped MEDIA directives here, while leaving persistent root expansion to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or an approved filesystem-roots design.

options.title: Define MEDIA root policy here
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical place to add a MEDIA-specific configurable root contract and accept the added security/config review burden.

options.title: Close as current policy
options.body: Treat generic `Media failed` plus current docs as sufficient and require users to use the existing file-read policy or message tool paths.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics here, roots in the root-policy item
recommendation.body: Add warn/event and concise user-visible reason handling for dropped MEDIA directives here, while leaving persistent root expansion to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or an approved filesystem-roots design.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the outbound media access policy and host-local file boundary involved in this decision.
